request.prompt:
Audit a proposed video QA adversarially. You see the QA, shuffled options, a separate visual answer, and the frames; NO GT. The proposed answer and blind answer can BOTH be wrong. Independently inspect the cited frames and actively seek a counterexample. Check component/tool identity, hand, temporal scope, actual transitions, physical vs printed objects, answer completeness, and each distractor. A plausible narrative or a legal frame ID is not visual proof. Tool pickup requires the same object on surface then lifted; state questions need actual connection evidence; observed order requires BOTH starts; an anomaly category requires a visible departure, not just normal handling. Do not certify internal fit, torque, mandatory order, or a correction without evidence.
Return exactly {"visual_grade":integer 0..3,"answer_supported":boolean,"blind_agrees":boolean,"question_unambiguous":boolean,"evidence_valid":boolean,"claim_checks":[{"claim_index":integer,"supported":boolean,"image_ids":[string],"observation":string}],"supported_option_indices":[integer],"option_checks":[{"index":integer,"verdict":"supported"|"contradicted"|"uncertain","reason":string}],"counterevidence":string,"before_id":string|null,"after_id":string|null}.
Grade3 means directly visible with no material ambiguity; lower grades are held. Give one claim_check per proposed claim, one option_check per option (zero-based index), <=25 words per observation/reason, counterevidence <=45 words. Cite only allowed exact frame IDs. List all visually supportable options, not just the most likely. Two supportable or any unresolved alternative means question ambiguity. A blank counterevidence string means none found; state real limitations otherwise. For tool pickup independently cite before/after IDs in chronological order; otherwise null allowed. Do not provide chain-of-thought.

payload.question: What types of error occurred while I was picking up the M4 nut with my right hand?

proposed_qa.open_question: What types of error occurred while I was picking up the M4 nut with my right hand?
proposed_qa.answer: Timing, spatial, object handling, and wrong part errors occurred during the action.
proposed_qa.mcq_question: Which option gives the complete set of error types while I was picking up the M4 nut with my right hand?

claims.claim: Timing, spatial, object handling, and wrong part errors occurred during the action.

options: Timing, spatial, object handling and procedural errors.
Timing, spatial, object handling and wrong tool errors.
Timing, spatial, object handling and wrong part errors.

blind_answer.answer: No visible error occurred; the person picked up a small component from the red tray with their right hand and placed it into the black object held in the left hand.
blind_answer.observation: The right hand reaches into the leftmost red tray, grasps a small metallic item, and transfers it to the black component held in the left hand.
blind_answer.limitation: The specific identity of the small item as an 'M4 nut' cannot be visually confirmed from the resolution provided.

claim_checks.observation: The action appears smooth and deliberate. No visible hesitation, drop, or incorrect part selection is evident in the provided frames.

option_checks.reason: No procedural error is visible; the user successfully transfers the component to the assembly.
No tool is used in this specific action, so a 'wrong tool' error is impossible.
The user picks up a component and inserts it. There is no visual evidence of picking up the wrong part.

result.counterevidence: The frames show a successful, uninterrupted transfer of a small component from the tray to the assembly. The proposed errors (timing, spatial, wrong part) are not visually supported by the smooth motion.
